definitions.explanation: Describes an older style, model, or method that has been superseded by newer ones. Often used for machines and equipment, and frequently with の before a noun.

examples.japanese: この{機械|きかい}は{旧式|きゅうしき}だ。
examples.english: This machine is an old model.

examples.japanese: {旧式|きゅうしき}のパソコンを{使|つか}っている。
{旧式|きゅうしき}のやり{方|かた}では{時間|じかん}がかかりすぎる。
examples.english: The old-fashioned method takes too much time.

notes:
Composed of {旧|きゅう} (old, former) + {式|しき} (style, type). It describes a model, design, or method from an earlier generation, now considered outdated. Frequently used with の before a noun ({旧式|きゅうしき}の{機械|きかい}).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {旧式|きゅうしき}の{機械|きかい}: an old-model machine
- {旧式|きゅうしき}のやり{方|かた}: an old-fashioned method

ANTONYM:
- {新式|しんしき}: new-style, new model — the opposite, a newer design or method
